title: Not-quite-human tastes: the stylized omnivorousness of LLM survey surrogates.

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing age-taste association coefficients from LLM-generated survey responses against ground-truth human data using mixed-effects meta-regression.
Comparing logged income-taste association coefficients between LLM surrogates and human survey data to identify retrograde class-based taste homologies.
Evaluating gender-taste association coefficients in LLM survey responses compared to human baselines to detect exaggerated and caricatured gender stereotypes.
Assessing race-taste association coefficients from synthetic samples against human survey data to detect exaggerated or fabricated racialization of music preferences.

Analyzing overall cultural taste inflation and 'WEIRD' alignment bias by calculating the Jaccard distance between synthetic survey responses and true human respondent tastes across various demographic groups.
